The steps of the Load Data wizard

Source: R/wizard-step_status.R
wizard_step_defs.Rd

The definition of the wizard's seven steps, in the order the user goes through them: Upload Data, Data Quality, Survey Files, National Rates, Shapefile, Map Survey Files and Map Shapefile Names. compute_step_states() turns it into the state of each step for a dataset. Survey Files and Shapefile are optional; the other five are required.

Usage

wizard_step_defs

Format

A list of seven lists, one per step. Each has:

  • key: the step's key, a string: "upload", "quality", "survey_files", "national_rates", "shapefile", "survey_mapping" or "map_mapping".

  • title_key: the translation key of the step's title.

  • required: TRUE when the step must be complete before the user can go on.

  • complete_fn: a function of the dataset that returns TRUE when the step is complete (see step_upload_complete()).

  • touched_fn (the Shapefile step only): a function of the dataset that returns TRUE when the user has done something on the step.

  • relevant_fn (the two mapping steps only): a function of the dataset whose result compute_step_states() reports as relevant.

Details

Survey Files comes before National Rates because an uploaded national survey fills in most of the National Rates fields; the user then only has to check them.

Examples

vapply(wizard_step_defs, function(s) s$key, character(1))
#> [1] "upload"         "quality"        "survey_files"   "national_rates"
#> [5] "shapefile"      "survey_mapping" "map_mapping"   
vapply(wizard_step_defs, function(s) s$required, logical(1))
#> [1]  TRUE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE

# test one step on a dataset
cache <- load_cache_data(system.file("extdata", "kenya.xlsx", package = "cd2030.core"))
#> ℹ Loading Excel "kenya.xlsx" for parts
#> ! The following columns are empty: anc_1trimester, under5_deaths, total_deaths,
#>   ipv2, measles_cases
#> ℹ Successfully loaded and cleaned data
#> ℹ Auto-detect candidates (|group|): vaccine=19, rmncah=28 -> selected rmncah
wizard_step_defs[[1]]$complete_fn(cache)
#> [1] TRUE
